listening.title: Interview question: tell me about a failure

lines.speaker: Linh (HR Manager)
lines.text: Nam, tell me about a time when a project of yours failed.

lines.speaker: Nam (Candidate)
lines.text: Last year I led a small website project for a retail client.

lines.speaker: Nam (Candidate)
lines.text: I was the project lead, so I agreed the schedule with the client myself.

lines.speaker: Nam (Candidate)
lines.text: I accepted an unrealistic timeline, and then we had serious scope creep.

lines.speaker: Nam (Candidate)
lines.text: We had a missed deadline of three weeks, and the client was unhappy.

lines.speaker: Linh (HR Manager)
lines.text: What did you do when you saw the problem?

lines.speaker: Nam (Candidate)
lines.text: I owned up to it early, showed the real numbers and offered a new plan.

lines.speaker: Linh (HR Manager)
lines.text: And what did you learn from that experience?

lines.speaker: Nam (Candidate)
lines.text: I learned the hard way never to over-promise, so I proposed a process improvement.

questions.q: What was Nam's role in the project?
What were the two main causes of the failure?
options: A small budget and a sick colleague
An unrealistic timeline and scope creep

questions.q: What did Nam do when he saw the problem?
options: He waited until the client asked
He asked another team to take over
He owned up to it early and offered a new plan

shadowing: In my last project, I set an unrealistic timeline and the team fell behind.
I owned up to the mistake and explained the delay to my manager quickly.
The main cause was scope creep, because we accepted new requests every single week.
After that failure, I proposed a small process improvement for planning and change requests.
I learned the hard way never to over-promise a date without checking with everyone.
